title: 2027-09-30 Steerline Brief and Mission Calibration
recorded_header: Date: 2027-09-30 | Start: 10:00 AM UTC | End: 11:02 AM UTC | Duration: 62 minutes | Location: Zoom - All Hands Stream
summary: Quarterly steerline: product milestones, incident learnings, hiring signal, and mission calibration. Leadership reviewed roadmap shifts, FY28 headcount cadence, and a simplified ops playbook. Q&A ended with concrete follow-ups on budgets and new on-call cadence.
topics: Recent P0 incident debrief and reliability program
Hiring and org changes through Q1 FY28
Commercial motion adjustments and go-to-market signals
action_items: Samir Khan: publish incident RCA and runbook updates by 2027-10-04
Janelle Ortiz: update product roadmap doc with latency-first plan and share deck link by 2027-10-06
Luis Gomez: circulate revised hiring cadence and interview rubric by 2027-10-08
Aisha Bennett: propose new on-call rotations and SLO targets by 2027-10-05
next_steps: Leadership to post the updated FY28 budget scenarios to internal drive (link in chat)
Schedule deep-dive sessions: infra perf workshop (invite to infra teams next week)
People team to run pulse survey and summarize results in two weeks
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Okay, good morning everyone, thanks for joining. We'll start the steerline brief. I'm gonna run through a quick set of updates and then Connor and Samir will take the incident and technical plan. Janelle will show the product calibration. Uh, try to keep the Q and A to the end.

[00:25] Connor Reid: Morning. Quick head start — we did see spiky latency last week, P0, uh caused by a KV cache eviction and a bad autoscaler loop. There was an interaction between the burst policy and the Dedicated pool. We rolled back the autoscaler, mitigated with a hotfix, and put throttles in the routing layer.

[00:48] Samir Khan: Yeah to add, the root cause had two parts: a sudden shift in seq length distribution from a partner test, and a GC thundering herd on a couple of nodes. The tracing was helpful but the alert noise made it harder to find the true signal.

[01:10] Janelle Ortiz: On the product side, we're changing the priority: latency-first for critical routes. That means we will push caching and smaller model variants into canary earlier, and make batching more aggressive for non-interactive endpoints. We'll iterate over the next 6 weeks.

[01:35] Maya Patel: Important we keep reliability while we optimize cost; the thesis hasn't changed but serving must be predictable. Any questions on that motion?

[02:00] 
[02:03] Staff Question (Speaker 1): Hey, is the Dedicated fallback still automatic to hosted variants, or will it be manual during the canary?

[02:15] Connor Reid: Right now fallback is policy-driven; during the canary we'll pin the fallback to a vetted variant so there's no surprise model swap. We'll document that in the rollout playbook.

[02:34] Samir Khan: Also note — KV cache is spelled K V cache in ops notes sometimes, and the log parsers mis-handle underscores, so there was a poor alert tie back. We'll normalize naming in the telemetry pipeline.

[02:56] Maya Patel: Good. Hiring — Luis, two minutes?

[03:05] Luis Gomez: Yeah, quick. We approved 22 roles for FY28 but pushing some into Q3/Q4 to balance burn. We'll prioritize reliability, infra, and a small customer success expansion. Details to follow in the hiring cadence doc. Also rolling out a new interview rubric focusing on systems thinking and collaboration.

[03:34] Audience noise / laughter / crosstalk

[04:00] Aisha Bennett: On on-call changes: proposed move to 4-week rotations and a dedicated second-on that's purely escalation, not hot-fixes. We want to reduce paging fatigue. We'll pilot for two cycles.

[04:22] Maya Patel: Okay that's great. Budget — the board wants three scenarios: conservative, base, aggressive. We'll submit by Oct 12. This affects hiring timing.

[04:40] Janelle Ortiz: Product roadmap snippet — shifting three deliverables. 1) Low-latency routing (Q4), 2) Prefix/KV cache enhancements (Q4), 3) Visibility + per-route cost telemetry (Q1). We'll share a deck after the meeting. Link: internal://docs/roadmap/steerline-sep-2027 (note: placeholder).

[05:10] 
[05:12] Employee (Speaker 2): Quick question on partner tests — the partner that spiked seq lengths, are we limiting test traffic model-wise?

[05:20] Samir Khan: Yes, there's a new contract gate for partner experiments. They need to run in a sandbox with quotas. We'll enforce by policy.

[05:40] Maya Patel: On the people side, small ask — managers, please schedule 1:1s focusing on workload and burnout prevention. Luis will run a pulse next week.

[06:02] 
[06:05] Audience: tiny noise, unclear

[06:15] Connor Reid: Ops playbook highlights: 1) Emergency rollback steps, 2) Hotfix checklist, 3) Clear owner matrix. All of these will be in a single doc and in the incident channel.

[06:39] Samir Khan: We also plan to harden kernel selection heuristics for quantized models; the perf delta was small but stable, and we can get cost wins for Dedicated customers.

[07:00] Janelle Ortiz: Commercial update: we're seeing enterprise interest in Private deployments, with extra requests for KMS and longer RPOs. Solutions team will prioritize security docs early.

[07:20] Maya Patel: We should aim to standardize our response: a single security brief for sales. Whoever's owning that — please coordinate with solutions.

[07:35] Luis Gomez: People ops note — new parental leave policy rollout, details in HR hub. Also flexible remote stipend approved.

[08:00] 
[08:05] Audience Question (Speaker 3): Will the new on-call change the compensation model for rotation?

[08:13] Aisha Bennett: We're proposing a 30% on-call stipend restructured to be less frequent but more meaningful. More in the policy doc.

[08:30] 
[08:33] Maya Patel: Okay, open Q&A. Please keep questions high-level.

[08:40] Employee (Speaker 4): For the infra perf workshop — will there be hands-on benchmarks we can run?

[08:47] Connor Reid: Yes, planning a sandbox with a set of traces and a benchmark harness. We'll publish instructions and a small dataset (anonymized). Expect to run a local pass if you want.

[09:05] Employee (Speaker 5): Any change to RBAC around rollout? We had some friction last week.

[09:12] Samir Khan: We'll centralize rollout permissions and add a temporary approval flow for canaries. That should reduce friction.

[09:28] 
[09:30] Maya Patel: All right let's do a quick recap. Connor?

[09:34] Connor Reid: Recap: incident RCA coming, throttle and fallback policy adjusted, canary plan pinned, perf workshop next week.

[09:44] Janelle Ortiz: Product: latency-first, roadmap updates and deck to follow.

[09:50] Samir Khan: Eng: on-call pilot and kernel heuristics for quantized paths.

[09:56] Luis Gomez: People: hiring cadence and pulse survey.

[10:00] Maya Patel: Next steps — leadership will post materials, action items have owners. We'll meet again for the infra deep dive in 7 days. Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.

[10:15] 
[10:20] System note: recording saved to /internal/recordings/2027-09-30-steerline.mp4
